items.headline: adidas made a dressy sneaker for 'Spezial' days
items.caption: The Albrecht II SPZL mixes a Freizeit runner with a Wallabee.
body: It has aged-look leather and a thick rubber sole.
It sits between everyday and smart.
How to wear it: with pleated trousers and a knit.

items.headline: An all-black Air Jordan 17 with stingray leather
items.caption: The 'Black Pack' Jordan 17 Low keeps branding quiet.
body: Matte black, patent touches and stingray texture.
It's the fourth shoe in the luxe black series.
How to wear it: all black, head to toe.

items.headline: Vans' waterproof Half Cab for winter
items.caption: A light grey GORE-TEX version of the classic skate shoe.
body: It's built to keep rain out.
Tonal grey keeps it clean.
How to wear it: with cargo trousers and a rain shell.

items.headline: Celine x Reebok: your first grown-up sneaker
items.caption: Celine's first Reebok shoe updates the slim Freestyle.
body: GQ says it's better made and less obvious than canvas trainers.
It's from creative director Michael Rider.
How to wear it: with tailored trousers.

items.headline: 17 sneakers that can handle rain and snow
items.caption: From GORE-TEX Air Max 95s to waterproof Salomon XT-6s.
body: Many are favourites with weatherproof upgrades.
No more wet socks.
How to wear it: pick one in a dark colour for daily use.

items.headline: How Robert Pattinson's beige suits were made for 'Primetime'
items.caption: Costume designer Alex Bovaird on boxy jackets and purple shirts.
body: He plays a mid-2000s US TV presenter.
The suits were his character's armour.
Style lesson: commit fully to one colour.

items.headline: Esquire's want list: Balenciaga's Le City turns 25
items.caption: The weekly roundup of what to wear, buy and do.
body: Balenciaga's cult Le City bag celebrates 25 years.
It's out as Martine Rose takes over the house.
Style lesson: one classic bag beats five trendy ones.

items.headline: Party blazers and Esquire editors' favourite new launches
items.caption: Plus a La Marzocco espresso machine inspired by a Porsche 911.
body: Esquire's weekly pick of new products.
Party season is coming.
How to wear it: a velvet blazer over a black tee.

items.headline: What Martine Rose could bring to Balenciaga
items.caption: The London designer already worked at Balenciaga under Demna.
body: She replaces Pierpaolo Piccioli.
Esquire says the choice makes total sense.
Watch for: sharp, street-smart menswear.

items.headline: Rexhep Rexhepi wins watchmaking's top prize
items.caption: His RRCHF took the Aiguille d'Or at the 2026 GPHG in Geneva.
body: Louis Vuitton, Otsuka Lotec and Baltic also won categories.
The GPHG is watchmaking's biggest awards night.
Style lesson: small makers can beat big brands.

items.headline: Chile's Atacama Desert bursts into bloom
items.caption: El Niño rains brought its biggest flower display in decades.
body: One of the driest places on Earth is now pink, yellow and purple.
The rare event wakes up insects and wildlife too.

items.headline: Sniffer dogs can find invasive plants
items.caption: Volunteer dog teams in Germany found them with 75% accuracy.
body: Invasive plants are a major cause of biodiversity loss.
Dogs offer a cheaper way to spot them early.

items.headline: She kept a stranger's coat for 30 years, then found him
items.caption: A Japanese teen gave his coat to a Korean girl after a racist attack.
body: Her school uniform had been slashed.
Three decades later, the coat went back to Norihisa Koyama.
